title: Magadha - Haryanka dynasty
capsule: The Haryanka dynasty was the founding ruling house of the Magadha kingdom in the central Gangetic plain, traditionally dated from around the mid-sixth century BCE. Bimbisara (c. 543–491 BCE) established systematic administration—appointing village headmen and executive officers—and expanded Magadha's reach through alliance and conquest, including a marriage alliance with the Licchavi republic of Vaishali. His son Ajatashatru (c. 491–461 BCE) extended the kingdom further, constructing the fortified outpost at Pataliputra and defeating both Vaishali and Kashi in prolonged campaigns. The dynasty ended when Ajatashatru's descendants were overthrown by the Shishunaga dynasty, probably around 413 BCE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynasty's dates and sequence depend heavily on Buddhist texts (the Mahavamsa) and diverge across traditions by several decades; territorial extent is inferred from later Magadha records and is only broadly known.
